macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Asian stocks rise as soft U.S. jobs data lowers rate-hike pressure
items.summary: Asian equities advanced after weaker-than-expected U.S. labor data reduced expectations for near-term Fed tightening. Reuters also said the S&P 500, Euro STOXX 50, FTSE 100, and Nikkei 225 were higher, with the Nikkei up 1.81%.

items.title: BOJ debate points toward a stronger case for a September rate hike
items.summary: Reuters reported that the Bank of Japan’s July meeting summary showed a growing chorus of policymakers arguing for a more forceful response to inflation risks, strengthening the case for a September rate increase. The report adds to pressure on Japanese bond and currency markets.

items.title: Japan posts first current account deficit in nearly 17 months
items.summary: Japan recorded a current account deficit in June for the first time in 17 months, according to finance ministry data cited by Reuters. The deficit was driven in part by larger dividend payouts from stronger overseas investment in domestic markets.

items.title: U.S. labor market shows further weakness in July
items.summary: MarketWatch reported that the U.S. unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while ADP said private employers added just 44,000 jobs in July, the smallest gain in six months. The soft labor data is reinforcing views that the Fed may stay patient on rates.

items.title: China inflation cools more than expected
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that China’s consumer and factory-gate prices both cooled more than expected in July, pointing to weak domestic demand. The data adds to concerns about the pace of China’s recovery and global growth demand.

items.title: Wall Street heads into inflation data with stocks near record levels
items.summary: Reuters said Wall Street is focused on upcoming inflation data to test whether the U.S. stock market’s recent record-setting run can continue and to gauge the Fed’s policy path. The report notes that U.S. stocks have been supported by expectations of less aggressive rate pressure.

items.title: Australia dollar softens as RBA expected to hold rates
items.summary: MarketScreener’s Reuters feed said the Australian dollar slipped after six weeks of gains, with markets expecting the Reserve Bank of Australia to leave rates unchanged. The same feed highlighted weaker China data and pressure in Australia’s mortgage market.

items.title: Oil and precious metals trade mixed amid Gulf uncertainty
items.summary: Reuters-linked market coverage showed Brent and WTI slightly lower, while gold drifted down from a seven-week high ahead of U.S. inflation data. The move reflects a market balancing geopolitics, inflation concerns, and expectations for central bank policy.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $65,000 as U.S. jobs miss lifts risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $65,000 after a weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs report boosted expectations for looser monetary conditions. The move was one of the most notable price developments in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin and ether ETFs post $1.1 billion inflow week
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin and ether ETFs recorded their best inflow week since April, drawing about $1.1 billion despite relatively low trading volume. The strong demand is a major institutional market signal.

items.title: U.S. Senate cloture filed on CLARITY Act, setting up September vote
items.summary: Senate Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on the CLARITY Act, advancing a key crypto market structure bill toward a Senate vote on Sept. 15. The development is one of the most significant U.S. regulatory updates in the past day.

items.title: U.S. sanctions two Iranian crypto exchanges in new enforcement push
items.summary: U.S. authorities sanctioned two additional Iranian crypto exchanges as part of an enforcement campaign targeting alleged sanctions evasion and money laundering. The action adds to the day’s most important regulatory headlines.

items.title: Australia orders Cryptolink Bitcoin ATMs offline over reporting failures
items.summary: Australia’s AUSTRAC suspended Cryptolink’s registration, forcing 96 Bitcoin ATMs offline over what regulators described as basic reporting failures. The move highlights ongoing scrutiny of crypto cash-access infrastructure.

items.title: Brazil introduces 24-hour hold on crypto transfers over $10,000
items.summary: Brazil’s central bank issued a rule requiring certain crypto transfers to self-custody wallets and foreign platforms to be delayed for up to 24 hours, starting in 2027. The policy is a notable new compliance measure in one of Latin America’s largest markets.

items.title: Bitcoin BIP-110 split widens as minority chain falls further behind
items.summary: Bitcoin’s BIP-110 proposal continued to split the network, with the minority chain losing momentum as the main network pulled ahead. The development is the most notable protocol-level story among blockchain projects in the last 24 hours.

items.title: BTCPay warns of actively exploited vulnerability that could drain funds
items.summary: BTCPay warned of a critical vulnerability being actively exploited, with attackers reportedly able to steal credentials and move funds. The incident is a major security development for Bitcoin payment infrastructure.

items.title: Bybit wins U.S. court support to trace funds from $1.5 billion hack
items.summary: A U.S. court backed Bybit’s bid to trace funds linked to the massive North Korea-related hack, improving prospects for asset recovery. This is one of the most notable legal and security-related project developments of the day.

items.title: Trump Media and Crypto.com end partnership ties
items.summary: Trump Media and Crypto.com ended their partnership arrangements as both companies shifted priorities. The breakup is a significant deal-side development for the broader crypto industry.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic tightens Claude biology safeguards after testing cuts false positives
items.summary: Anthropic said it updated Claude Fable 5’s biology safeguards to reduce false positives, cutting biology-related fallback responses by about 85% in testing across product surfaces. The move reflects an industry trend toward more targeted AI safety controls rather than broad refusals.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Code beta, a terminal coding agent
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Code in beta, a terminal-based coding agent powered by Muse Spark 1.2. The release highlights continued competition in developer-focused AI tools and lower-priced coding model offerings.

items.title: OpenAI slows Astra model development over security concerns
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly slowed work on its Astra model because of cybersecurity concerns. The development underscores how security review is shaping frontier-model deployment timelines.

items.title: OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide
items.summary: OpenAI acquired presentation startup NextSlide, whose team is now working on ChatGPT. The deal suggests OpenAI is continuing to add product and workflow features around its consumer AI platform.

items.title: ChatGPT expands access with unlimited text chats for free users
items.summary: OpenAI said ChatGPT free and Go users are now getting unlimited text chats, along with a new think button for complex queries. The change points to broader access and more usage-focused product packaging.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf browser for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents rather than humans. The launch adds to a growing trend of infrastructure and browser tools built specifically for autonomous agent workflows.

items.title: Google Maps adds agentic features for ordering and bookings
items.summary: Google Maps is adding agentic features that include food ordering and hotel bookings. The update shows major platforms turning consumer apps into AI-assisted task completion tools.

items.title: Anthropic to turn Claude Code Auto Mode on by default
items.summary: Anthropic will turn Claude Code’s Auto Mode on by default for Pro, Max, and Team users starting August 14. The change reduces manual approval prompts and signals growing confidence in guarded agentic coding workflows.

items.title: Nvidia-linked AI infrastructure deals expand in Asia and the U.S.
items.summary: Reports this week highlighted major AI infrastructure financing and expansion, including Ooredoo, Nvidia, Nokia, and Indosat launching Indonesia’s first dedicated AI compute and neocloud platform, and separate reports that Nvidia may invest up to $3 billion in Stargate data center developer Lancium. These deals reflect continued heavy investment in AI compute capacity.

items.title: Chinese AI chip access is facing new U.S. scrutiny
items.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department’s BIS is reviewing how Chinese AI companies access Nvidia chips overseas, including through legally rented foreign data centers. The reported review signals tighter export-control enforcement around advanced AI hardware.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA completes $20 billion buyout, ending its public-company era
items.summary: Electronic Arts was acquired by a group of investors in a deal that closed this week, adding about $20 billion in debt to the company. The transaction is one of the biggest gaming-industry developments in the last 24 hours and is expected to reshape EA’s strategy and spending.

items.title: Sony warns PS5 buyers that new physical games may disappear in 2028
items.summary: Sony has reportedly added warning labels on PS5 boxes with disc drives, indicating that new physical game releases are expected to end in 2028. The move has intensified discussion about the industry’s shift away from discs and toward digital distribution.

items.title: Nintendo reports physical games still account for 38.5% of game revenue
items.summary: Nintendo’s latest quarterly figures show that physical editions still make up a substantial share of its game revenue. The update comes amid broader industry debate over the future of discs and cartridges.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly lays off staff at Halo Studios after Campaign Evolved debut
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft has cut employees at Halo Studios shortly after the debut of Halo: Campaign Evolved. If confirmed, the move would add to a run of studio and workforce changes across the games business.

items.title: Free Quake expansion released for the remaster
items.summary: Microsoft released a free expansion for the Quake remaster, marking a notable retro-game update and anniversary-style content drop. The new add-on adds fresh content to a classic shooter that remains active decades after launch.

items.title: GTA VI news cycle heats up with new footage timing and preorder buzz
items.summary: Recent gaming coverage says new Grand Theft Auto VI footage is expected to debut later this month, while preorder interest for the game is described as exceptionally strong. The continued focus on GTA VI remains one of the biggest release stories in gaming.

items.title: Minecraft is coming to Switch 2 in October
items.summary: Minecraft is slated to launch on the Switch 2 in October, adding another major third-party title to Nintendo’s new hardware lineup. The release is one of the clearest recent examples of cross-generation support for the platform.
